title: Give each acceptance a legacy id of the form AC-{STEP}-{NNN}

facts.note: Acceptance definition files are identifiable by kind/path.
Fires when an acceptance is authored or its identity is edited.
Needs a diff-level observer detecting changes to identity.id of an acceptance.

fires: Planner writes a new acceptance and must fill identity.id
Planner renames or renumbers an acceptance's identity.id
Planner moves an acceptance to a different step and the step code in its id must change
doesNotFire: Editing only the acceptance URN (governed by the URN-generation convention)
Editing acceptance body text without touching identity.id
Authoring wagons, WMBTs or docs that contain no acceptance identity

given: You are authoring or editing an acceptance and setting its identity.id (the legacy id, kept for backward compatibility).
then: Write identity.id as AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, where {STEP} is the step code mapped from the step name (define→DEF, locate→LOC, prepare→PREP, confirm→CONF, execute→EXEC, monitor→MON, modify→MOD, resolve→RES, conclude→CONC) and {NNN} is the number, e.g. AC-EXEC-201, AC-CONF-004.
prefer: Derive {STEP} strictly from the step_code mapping (step-name → id code) rather than abbreviating the step name ad hoc.
Keep {NNN} as a three-digit number as in the canonical examples (AC-EXEC-201, AC-CONF-004).
avoid: Using full step names or non-mapped abbreviations in the id (e.g. AC-EXECUTE-…, AC-CFG-…).
Treating the legacy AC id as a replacement for the acceptance URN; it is a parallel, backward-compatibility identifier.
why: The legacy AC id is kept in identity.id for backward compatibility.
evidence: identity.id of each acceptance matches AC-{STEP}-{NNN} with {STEP} one of DEF, LOC, PREP, CONF, EXEC, MON, MOD, RES, CONC.
{STEP} equals the step_code mapped from the acceptance's step name.
verifier_detail: step_code term (step-name -> id code): define=DEF, locate=LOC, prepare=PREP, confirm=CONF, execute=EXEC, monitor=MON, modify=MOD, resolve=RES, conclude=CONC.
